name: Crude oil
blurb: The largest physical commodity trade by value and volume; most of it moves by tanker.

name: Refined products
blurb: Diesel/gasoil, gasoline, jet fuel, fuel oil and naphtha shipped from refining hubs to deficit regions.

name: LNG
blurb: Liquefied natural gas, shipped in cryogenic carriers from liquefaction plants to regasification terminals.

name: Natural gas
blurb: Gas production and pipeline trade; seaborne gas is covered under LNG.

name: LPG
blurb: Propane and butane, carried mainly by very large gas carriers from the US and Middle East to Asia.

name: Thermal coal
blurb: Steam coal burned for power; the largest dry bulk cargo after iron ore.

name: Uranium
blurb: Mined uranium for nuclear fuel; small tonnages, concentrated supply.

name: Iron ore
blurb: The largest dry bulk trade, dominated by Australia and Brazil shipping to China on Capesize vessels.

name: Metallurgical coal
blurb: Coking coal for blast-furnace steelmaking; Australia leads seaborne supply.

name: Steel
blurb: Crude steel production and the trade in semi-finished and finished steel.

name: Ferrous scrap
blurb: Recycled steel for the furnaces of steelmakers and foundries; the United States, the United Kingdom and Germany lead exports and Turkey leads imports.

name: Pig iron & DRI
blurb: Pig iron and direct-reduced iron, the iron units that steelmakers use besides scrap; Brazil and Russia lead pig iron exports, Oman and Russia lead direct-reduced iron.

name: Copper
blurb: Copper concentrate, blister and refined cathode; Chile, Peru and DR Congo supply, China smelts.

name: Aluminium
blurb: Primary aluminium smelted from alumina, power-intensive; China makes over half.

name: Bauxite & alumina
blurb: Aluminium ore and its refined oxide; Guinea and Australia are the main sources.

name: Nickel
blurb: Ore, ferro-nickel and nickel pig iron, intermediates and refined nickel; Indonesia now dominates mine supply.

name: Zinc
blurb: Zinc concentrate and refined metal, used mainly for galvanising steel.

name: Lead
blurb: Mostly used in batteries; much supply comes from recycling.

name: Tin
blurb: Solder metal; China and Indonesia mine the most, with Peru, Brazil and DR Congo next.

name: Lithium
blurb: Lithium carbonate and hydroxide for batteries, and the spodumene concentrate that hard-rock mines ship to China.

name: Cobalt
blurb: Battery and superalloy metal, overwhelmingly mined in DR Congo and refined in China.

name: Rare earths
blurb: Elements for magnets and catalysts; China dominates mining and separation.

name: Manganese
blurb: Ore for steel alloys and batteries; South Africa, Gabon and Australia lead.

name: Chromium
blurb: Chromite ore for ferro-chromium and stainless steel; South Africa supplies most of the world and China buys most of it.

name: Ferro-alloys
blurb: The ferro-alloys that steel is made with: ferro-chromium, ferro-manganese, silico-manganese, ferro-silicon and others; ferro-nickel is on the nickel page.

name: Molybdenum
blurb: Alloying metal for steels; China, Chile, the United States and Peru mine the most, and concentrates are traded.

name: Graphite
blurb: Natural graphite in flake and powder; China leads production and exports.

name: Gold
blurb: Mined gold and the bullion trade through refining and vaulting hubs.

name: Silver
blurb: Mostly a by-product of lead, zinc and copper mining; Mexico and Peru lead.

name: Platinum group metals
blurb: Platinum and palladium for autocatalysts; South Africa and Russia dominate.

name: Wheat
blurb: The most traded grain; Black Sea, EU, North America and Australia export.

name: Corn
blurb: Feed grain; the US, Brazil, Argentina and Ukraine supply most exports.

name: Barley
blurb: Feed and malting grain; Australia, the EU, Canada, Argentina and Russia lead exports.

name: Sorghum
blurb: Feed and food grain of hot, dry regions; the US, Australia, Brazil and Argentina supply the exports.

name: Soybeans
blurb: Brazil and the US ship most of the world's soybeans, largely to China.

name: Soybean meal
blurb: Protein meal from crushing; Argentina is the largest exporter.

name: Soybean oil
blurb: Vegetable oil from crushing, used for food and biofuel.

name: Rice
blurb: Mostly consumed where grown; India, Thailand and Vietnam lead exports.

name: Pulses
blurb: Dried peas, chickpeas, beans and lentils; Canada, Australia, Russia and Myanmar lead exports.

name: Sugar
blurb: Raw and white sugar; Brazil dominates exports.

name: Coffee
blurb: Green coffee beans; Brazil and Vietnam lead supply.

name: Cocoa
blurb: Cocoa beans, concentrated in Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana.

name: Cotton
blurb: Raw cotton fibre; the US, Brazil and Australia export, Asian mills import.

name: Palm oil
blurb: The most produced vegetable oil, almost all from Indonesia and Malaysia.

name: Sunflower
blurb: Seed, oil and meal; Ukraine and Russia supply most of the oil and meal in trade.

name: Rapeseed & canola
blurb: Oilseed grown in Canada, the EU and Australia, with its oil and meal.

name: Potash
blurb: Potassium fertiliser, as chloride and as sulphate; Canada, Russia and Belarus dominate.

name: Phosphate
blurb: Phosphate rock and the fertilisers and acid made from it: DAP, MAP, superphosphates and phosphoric acid; Morocco holds most reserves.

name: Urea & nitrogen
blurb: Nitrogen fertilisers made from natural gas: urea, ammonia, ammonium nitrate (pure and mixed with limestone), UAN and ammonium sulphate; Russia and the Gulf producers lead urea exports.

name: Sulphur
blurb: Sulphur recovered from oil and gas and mined, shipped in bulk to fertiliser and chemical makers.

name: NPK fertilisers
blurb: Compound fertilisers: the grades that carry all three nutrients, nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium (NPK), and those that carry two of them in one product.
